items.title: Yiddish speaker numbers
items.claim: Yiddish is a West Germanic language historically spoken by Ashkenazi Jews. About how many speakers worldwide today?
items.reveal_title: Around three quarters of a million today
items.reveal:
Ethnologue and YIVO estimates suggest between roughly 600,000 and 1 million speakers, concentrated in Hasidic communities in the US, Israel, the UK and elsewhere.

Before 1939, estimates suggested over 11 million speakers.
items.why: Catastrophic 20th-century events shaped which Germanic languages survived in numbers.

items.title: Where German is spoken
items.claim: German is an official or co-official language of how many European countries?

options.text: Six (Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Belgium)

items.reveal_title: Six European states give German official status
items.reveal:
It is the sole official language in Liechtenstein and one of multiple in Belgium (East Cantons), Luxembourg, Switzerland and Italy's South Tyrol.

German is the most widely spoken native language in the EU (around 95 million).
items.why: Language geography rarely matches state borders neatly.

items.title: The longest German word in use
items.claim: German allows long noun compounds. A famous legal-administrative example abolished in 2013 was:
items.reveal:
The cattle-marking-and-beef-labelling-supervision-duties-delegation-law was repealed in 2013, partially because EU rules changed.

The Duden does not generally treat such legal compounds as 'words' for dictionary purposes.
items.why: Morphological possibility is not the same as everyday usage.
